name: Ring Push-Up in Weighted Vest
description: A ring push-up performed while wearing a weighted vest, distributing additional load evenly across the torso. Unlike attaching weight to a belt, the vest allows full natural movement of the arms and rings without the load shifting. The rings create an unstable hand surface that maximizes stabilizer demand, while the vest provides simple, clean progressive overload for the pectoralis major and triceps beyond bodyweight capacity.

execution.starting_position: Put on a weighted vest and secure it comfortably. Set rings low enough for push-up position (15–30 cm off the ground). Get into push-up position with hands in the rings.
execution.setup_instructions: Secure the vest before setting up in the ring position. Ensure the vest does not shift during the movement. Set rings at appropriate height. Progress from lighter vest loads, adding 5 kg increments.
steps: Step 1: Establish a stable plank with hands in rings. The vest distributes additional load across the torso.
Step 2: Lower the chest toward the ring level, managing the ring instability.
Step 3: Descend until chest is at ring height.
Step 4: Press powerfully to full arm extension. Turn rings out at the top for shoulder stability.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on descent, exhale on press.
common_mistakes: Vest that shifts or rides up — a poorly fitted vest disrupts balance
Adding too much vest weight before the movement is mastered unweighted
Rings swinging out of control due to inability to stabilize the extra load
safety_considerations: Master bodyweight ring push-ups before adding vest weight
Start with 5–10 kg vest and progress conservatively
Have a training partner observe during the first loaded set
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full push-up range, chest to ring level at the bottom, complete lockout at top.
coaching_cues: Turn the rings outward at the top — this external rotation is a key shoulder safety cue
Press the rings apart slightly to engage serratus and stabilize the shoulder
